text: Every transaction this course has sent needed gas in the sending wallet. For a brand-new user, that's a real onboarding barrier. Gasless means the user doesn't have to hold the token to pay for it themselves.
A user signs an intent off-chain, not a transaction. A relayer wraps it into a real transaction, pays gas, and submits it. The contract verifies the user's signature, not the relayer's identity.
Inside a relayed call, msg.sender is the relayer's address, not the user's. ERC-2771's trusted-forwarder pattern fixes that — _msgSender extracts the real user's address instead.
A relayer is a real backend service verifying signatures, paying real gas from its own funded wallet, and deciding what it's willing to sponsor at all.

That closes this course — the off-chain half of a dApp. Next in the Blockchain Engineer path: DeFi and Token Engineering, building on these same backend patterns for tokens, liquidity, and DeFi protocols.
